title: Same-size rewrites in the middle of files larger than the head and tail windows, one ending with an incomplete line; then a larger rewrite
policy: P13 (#56 policy): a file whose change time moved while its observed size didn't is read again from the start, whatever its anchors say; that size is the one observed last time, not the saved offset, which is short of it when the last line is incomplete. A larger rewrite is read again when the head, the tail or one of 16 sampled 4 KiB windows before the saved offset changed.
derivation: Every record is [1, 0]. sa holds 120 records (about 25 KiB), sb 80 records (about 17 KiB) and an incomplete last line, which is pending (not counted, reported). Step 1: 200. Step 2: sa rewritten in place at the same size with record 60 replaced (M060): + 1; sb rewritten at the same size with record 40 replaced (N040) and the same incomplete line: + 1. Both edits are outside the first and the last 4 KiB before the saved offsets. 202. Step 3: sa rewritten larger: record 30 replaced (X030) and one record appended (E120). sa is about 25 KiB, so the 16 sampled windows cover all of it and the anchor changes: read again, + 2 = 204. Records already counted stay counted (P12). A fresh index of the final files: sa 121 + sb 80 = 201. Before the policy (1a7669c) step 2 added nothing (the anchors matched) and so did step 3's middle edit.
